title: Basil-Pistachio Aioli
description: Basil and smooth pistachio paste turn a garlic mayonnaise into a pale green sauce for poached cod or tender chicken.
equipment: Mortar and pestle or small food processor

ingredients.name: plain full-fat mayonnaise
ingredients.note: Use plain commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized eggs.

steps.title: Make the basil paste
steps.text: Tear {basil} into the mortar and work it with {lemon} and {garlic} for 1–2 minutes, until the leaves form a soft paste.

steps.title: Smooth the pistachio
steps.text: Stir {pistachio} into the herb paste. Loosen it with a spoonful of {mayo} until smooth.

steps.title: Fold the aioli
steps.text: Fold the pistachio mixture through the remaining mayonnaise just until the color is even.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Scrape all of the mixture into the measuring cup. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time if needed to reach about 1 cup, maintaining a smooth spoonable texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chill covered for 20 minutes. Spoon onto warm poached fish or swirl into a separate portion of thick gravy just before serving.

notes: Yield: About 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Prepare up to a day ahead and press a cover against the surface to protect the basil color. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Mayonnaise can split after freezing, and the fresh basil darkens. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir until smooth just before portioning. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw covered in the refrigerator, then whisk or blend briefly and serve cold. Option A uses lemon juice. For gentler Option B, use water for the lemon and halve the granulated garlic. The aioli is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 158 kcal, 0.8 g protein, 1.0 g total carbohydrate, 16.8 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 131 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
